name: Atlanta
operatingHours: MARTA rail runs ~4:45 AM–1:00 AM on weekdays and ~6:00 AM–1:00 AM on weekends and holidays (every ~10–12 min, ~20 min early, late and on weekends). The Atlanta Streetcar loops downtown ~6:00 AM–11:00 PM (to ~1:00 AM Fri–Sat, from ~9:00 AM Sun).
fareInfo: $2.50 per MARTA trip (2026), paid by tapping a contactless bank card or phone wallet at the gates, or a Breeze card or the Breeze app (new fare system since March 2026); transfers within 3 hours are free when you tap with the same card. Unlimited Breeze passes from 1 day (~$9) to 7 days (~$24). The Atlanta Streetcar has been fare-free in recent years.

sights.name: Georgia Aquarium
sights.note: One of the world's largest aquariums, where whale sharks and manta rays glide past a huge viewing window in the Ocean Voyager gallery, plus beluga whales, dolphin and sea lion shows.
sights.hours: Daily, usually ~9:00 AM–9:00 PM (varies by date; last entry 30 min before close)

sights.name: World of Coca-Cola
sights.note: The soft-drink giant's own museum on Pemberton Place, with the secret-formula vault, a vintage ad gallery and a tasting room pouring around 100 drinks from around the world.
sights.hours: Daily ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM, later on Fri–Sun (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas)

sights.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
sights.note: A 30-acre garden beside Piedmont Park with a treetop canopy walk, an orchid house, the Cascades Garden and giant living plant sculptures; the Garden Lights show runs on winter evenings.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–~7:00 PM (seasonal; closed Mon); Garden Lights evenings mid-Nov–mid-Jan

sights.name: Fox Theatre
sights.note: A lavish 1929 movie palace in Moorish and Egyptian style, with a starry 'night sky' ceiling, that now hosts Broadway tours and concerts; see it at a show or on a guided tour.
sights.hours: Open for performances; guided tours on select mornings (check schedule)

sights.name: Centennial Olympic Park
sights.note: The green heart of downtown, built for the 1996 Olympics, with the Fountain of Rings splash fountain and the aquarium, Coca-Cola museum and civil rights center on its edges. Free.

sights.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park
sights.note: Dr. King's Sweet Auburn neighbourhood: his birth home (reopened July 2026 after restoration), Ebenezer Baptist Church, the visitor center exhibits and the tomb he shares with Coretta Scott King. Free.
sights.hours: Visitor center daily ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM; birth home by free ranger-led tour, limited spaces

sights.name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
sights.note: A moving museum that links the American civil rights movement to today's global human rights struggles; its lunch-counter sit-in simulation is unforgettable. Reopened in 2025 after a major expansion.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sun 12:00–5:00 PM (last entry 4:00 PM; closed Mon)

sights.name: Zoo Atlanta
sights.note: A mid-sized zoo in historic Grant Park known for its large gorilla troop and giant pandas' legacy, plus elephants, tigers and a reptile house.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 9:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sat–Sun 9:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Piedmont Park
sights.note: Midtown's big park, with a lake, wide lawns facing the skyline, a Saturday green market and a link onto the BeltLine. Free.

sights.name: Atlanta History Center
sights.note: A 33-acre Buckhead campus with the restored Cyclorama battle painting, Civil War and Southern history galleries, the 1928 Swan House mansion and an 1860s farm.
sights.hours: Daily ~10:00 AM–5:30 PM, Sun from 12:00 PM

sights.name: High Museum of Art
sights.note: The Southeast's leading art museum, in white Richard Meier and Renzo Piano buildings, strong on American art, folk and self-taught artists, photography and major touring shows.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (Fri till 9:00 PM), Sun 12:00–5:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Jimmy Carter Presidential Library & Museum
sights.note: A museum of the 39th president's life, from Plains peanut farm to the White House and his Nobel Peace Prize work, with a full-size Oval Office replica and a Japanese garden.

sights.name: Ponce City Market
sights.note: A vast 1920s Sears warehouse reborn as a food hall and shopping hub on the BeltLine, with a rooftop fairground, mini-golf and skyline views.
sights.hours: Food hall daily ~8:00 AM–10:00 PM; rooftop hours vary

sights.name: Center for Puppetry Arts
sights.note: America's largest puppetry museum, home to the Jim Henson collection of Muppets alongside puppets from around the world, plus daily family shows.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri 9:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sat 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sun 12:00–5:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: Oakland Cemetery
sights.note: Atlanta's oldest cemetery, a Victorian garden of ornate mausoleums and old oaks where Margaret Mitchell and Maynard Jackson rest, with skyline views. Free to wander; guided tours on weekends.
sights.hours: Daily dawn–dusk (~8:00 AM–7:00 PM, earlier in winter)

sights.name: College Football Hall of Fame
sights.note: An interactive shrine to American college football with a wall of helmets from every school, game-day exhibits and an indoor field where you can try kicking and passing drills.
sights.hours: Daily 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (last ticket 4:30 PM; may close for events)

sights.name: Atlanta BeltLine Eastside Trail
sights.note: A popular paved walking and cycling path on an old rail corridor, lined with street murals, breweries and patios between Piedmont Park, Ponce City Market and Inman Park. Free.

sights.name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
sights.note: A historic municipal market from 1924 where butchers and produce stalls share space with soul food, Caribbean and other cheap lunch counters, a short walk from the King sites.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat ~8:00 AM–6:00 PM (vendor hours vary); limited on Sun

railStations.name: Peachtree Station
railStations.note: Atlanta's small Amtrak station on Peachtree Street in Brookwood Hills, served only by the Crescent (New York–Washington–Atlanta–New Orleans), one train each way daily. No MARTA rail link: Arts Center station is ~1.3 km away by bus 110, taxi or rideshare.
railStations.hours: Station open ~7:00 AM–9:30 PM; northbound Crescent departs mornings, southbound evenings.

airports.name: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport
airports.transitNote: MARTA's Red and Gold Lines (shown on map) start at Airport station, inside the Domestic Terminal by baggage claim, and reach Five Points in ~17 min and Midtown in ~25 min for the standard $2.50 fare. From the International Terminal, ride the free Plane Train to the Domestic Terminal. The free ATL SkyTrain links the terminal to the rental-car center and Gateway Center hotels.
airports.hours: First train ~4:45 AM (~6:00 AM weekends), last ~1:00 AM; no overnight trains.
